articles.summary: Millrose closed $1.0 billion of senior unsecured notes on Oct. 6, 2026: $500M 6.500% due 2029 and $500M 6.750% due 2031. The 2031 tranche must be redeemed at par if the Dream Finders/Beazer merger misses a May 13, 2027 deadline.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose's marginal unsecured funding cost is now 6.5% to 6.75%, a direct read on the floor under its option pricing, and half the raise was tied to land banking Dream Finders' Beazer deal.

articles.summary: On Aug. 27, 2026 Millrose amended its Founder's Rights Agreement with Lennar (Priority Amount for Lennar's capital priority right; its secured-financing collateral consent right) and its Kennedy Lewis management agreement (investment guidelines scope, reimbursable expenses). No figures disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: Changes to Lennar's priority claim on Millrose capital and to what Kennedy Lewis is allowed to invest in determine how much Millrose capacity is free to compete for Domain's other builders; the exhibits are worth reading.

suggested_update.text: On Aug. 27, 2026 Lennar and Millrose amended the Founder's Rights Agreement, adjusting the Priority Amount for Lennar's capital priority right and its secured-financing collateral consent right (amounts not stated in the 8-K body).

articles.summary: Millrose Q3 2026: net income $130.0M ($0.78/share), AFFO $0.80/share; board authorized a $250M buyback Oct. 26. After quarter-end it closed about $1.1B for Dream Finders' Beazer deal: roughly $580M land banking on about 7,000 homesites plus $488M of 12% preferred.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose is now about 42% outside Lennar across 21 other builders at a 10.8% weighted yield, and it used preferred equity alongside land banking to win Dream Finders, a structure Domain may be asked to match.

suggested_update.text: Millrose closed about $1.1B of capital support on Oct. 20, 2026 for the Beazer acquisition: about $580M of land banking across roughly 7,000 homesites plus about $488M of preferred equity at a 12% dividend.

articles.summary: Coverage of Millrose's Sept. 2026 launch of a $1B two-tranche notes offering; proceeds, with a $500M delayed-draw term loan, earmarked for homesite purchases tied to the Dream Finders/Beazer merger and paying down an $850M revolver balance.
articles.why_it_matters: Same Millrose notes deal as the closing 8-K; adds only that the revolver stood at $850M drawn before the raise, a sign of how stretched Millrose's short-term capacity was.

articles.summary: Millrose priced its $1.0B private notes offering on Sept. 22, 2026 at par: $500M 6.500% due 2029 and $500M 6.750% due 2031, with closing expected Oct. 6.
articles.why_it_matters: Pricing step of the same Millrose notes deal covered by the Oct. 6 closing 8-K; the coupons are the competitor cost-of-capital datapoint.

articles.summary: Millrose declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.79 per share on Class A and Class B stock, payable Oct. 15, 2026 to holders of record Oct. 5.
articles.why_it_matters: Routine payout; the only use to Domain is that Millrose's $0.79 dividend sets the return its option fees must keep covering.

articles.summary: News brief on the Nov. 3, 2026 Starwood Capital and Trez Capital partnership to make residential land acquisition and development loans in the US.
articles.why_it_matters: Same Starwood and Trez announcement as the full release; a new institutional lender against the land Domain's builders would otherwise option.

articles.summary: Starwood Capital and Trez Capital announced on Nov. 3, 2026 a partnership to originate land acquisition and development loans for US single-family communities, seeded with a $450M Trez loan portfolio and targeting more than $1B of originations a year.
articles.why_it_matters: Starwood is putting institutional capital behind A&D loans at $1B-plus a year, a debt alternative builders and developers can use instead of a Domain land bank; Anthony Murphy at Starwood and John Hutchinson at Trez lead it.

articles.summary: Millrose 10-Q for Sept. 30, 2026: homesites under option $9.90B (from $8.87B at year-end), Q3 option fee revenue $209.5M, net income $130.0M, corporate debt $3.13B, plus $332.7M of single-family rental homes carrying a $210.6M secured facility.
articles.why_it_matters: The balance sheet shows Millrose's optioned-homesite book grew about $1.0B in nine months and that it now holds rental homes on separate secured debt, both measures of how much capacity it has left to bid against Domain.

articles.summary: PIMCO Dynamic Income Fund prospectus supplement for a share offering; collected only because the text contains the phrase "land banking". Not opened.
articles.why_it_matters: A closed-end bond fund's routine share-sale document; nothing here about builder land capital that Domain could act on.

articles.summary: Syndicated summary of Millrose's Q3 2026 results: AFFO $0.80/share, net income $130M, new $250M buyback, Q4 AFFO outlook $0.82 to $0.84, and about $1.1B of capital for Dream Finders' Beazer acquisition.
articles.why_it_matters: Same Millrose Q3 results as the earnings 8-K; no added facts on pricing or capacity.

articles.summary: Millrose's Sept. 2026 release announcing the launch of a private offering of up to $1.0B of senior notes.
articles.why_it_matters: Launch step of the Millrose notes deal that the Oct. 6 closing 8-K reports in full with coupons and terms.

articles.summary: Weyerhaeuser's November 2026 investor presentation lists "land banking" once, as an emerging opportunity in its Strategic Land Solutions segment, with no definition, size or timeline; nothing on homebuilder lots.
articles.why_it_matters: A timberland owner using the phrase in passing; not a competitor for builder lot financing on anything shown here.

articles.summary: Brief on Millrose pricing $1B of senior notes: $500M of 6.500% notes due 2029 and a second $500M tranche.
articles.why_it_matters: Syndicated copy of the Millrose notes pricing; the closing 8-K is the source to read for competitor funding cost.

articles.summary: Texas County and District Retirement System committed $200M to TPG Essential Housing IV, a TPG Angelo Gordon closed-end fund seeking $3B of equity; Kern County's pension committed $50M in August.
articles.why_it_matters: TPG Angelo Gordon is raising a $3B fourth Essential Housing fund and pensions are writing $200M tickets, which means more competing land-bank capital chasing the same builders and the same LPs Domain courts.

articles.summary: Five Point Q3 2026: net loss $4.4M, 2026 net income guidance cut to about $20M as land sales slip. Its Hearthstone unit, which manages residential land banking funds, reports about $3.4B under management and $6.5M of quarterly fee revenue.
articles.why_it_matters: Hearthstone is a rival land-bank manager; $3.4B under management and Five Point's stated push to grow its fee income mark it as a smaller competitor still looking to add builder deals.

articles.summary: Summary of Millrose's Sept. 22, 2026 pricing of a $1.0B two-tranche private senior notes offering.
articles.why_it_matters: Syndicated copy of the Millrose notes pricing; nothing beyond the closing 8-K.

articles.summary: Brief on Millrose pricing $1.0B of senior notes in two equal $500M tranches.
articles.why_it_matters: Syndicated copy of the Millrose notes pricing; nothing beyond the closing 8-K.

articles.summary: Scott Cox of SLC Advisors expects 2027 to bring land re-trades and real price cuts, with builders refusing roughly 10% land-bank carry and pushing slower takedowns. He predicts Millrose will cut option fees and ease takedowns to keep assets.
articles.why_it_matters: An opinion piece, but it is the argument builders' land teams will bring to Domain in 2027: lower option fees, softer takedowns, and a claim that Millrose's asset-based fee makes it concede first.

articles.summary: The Real Deal reports Millrose bought about 1,200 single-family homes from Lennar to run as rentals, disclosed with Q3 results amid a lawsuit over the matter. Millrose's release puts it at 1,233 homes in 18 states for about $333M.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose is taking finished homes off Lennar's hands, a service beyond lot options that Domain does not offer Lennar, and the related-party deal is drawing litigation that could constrain how Millrose deals with its founder.

suggested_update.text: In Q3 2026 Lennar sold 1,233 completed single-family homes in 18 states to Millrose for about $333M, to be held as rentals (per Millrose's Oct. 27, 2026 results release).
